geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the threshold from a pure cantilever into a lifted ground-edge articulation that better supports an active entry seam.
Bind the lifted threshold to the access edge for a clear public response.
Keep the lift modest so the dominant mass remains compact and continuous.
Expand the carved void into a more usable court while preserving the main body.
Maintain the void opening toward the verified access side.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the public threshold from a simple cantilever into a clearer lifted edge that better reads as occupied ground response to access.
Bring the threshold articulation slightly earlier so the opening reads more deliberately at the frontage.
Increase the horizontal pull of the public edge articulation without changing the dominant compact mass.
Slightly enlarge the court/void so it reads as a more usable public space rather than a narrow subtraction.
Keep the void aligned to the verified access side so the public opening remains legible to the street.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent compact neighborhood building: one dominant rectilinear mass with a strong carved central void and an upper horizontal gesture. The top and oblique views confirm the same organization, so it is not coherent in only one view. The void is legible and public-facing, and it gives the street edge an address rather than sealing the site. The massing still feels somewhat generic and box-derived, with only modest section articulation, so the silhouette is serviceable rather than exceptional. Programmatically it can plausibly support neighborhood living or mixed neighborhood uses because it has an active ground response, a clear public void, and calm upper massing; it does not read like a gym, tower, or large-span hall.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion/cultural than neighborhood-living; avoid copying the curved roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a central void and an upper connector can support a public threshold without losing mass unity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more complex than the candidate; tower-podium emphasis is not transferable here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like courtyard organization and stepped lower blocks can preserve openness while maintaining hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More civic and polished than the candidate; do not imitate facade transparency.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A rectangular volume with a large carved void and overhang creates a legible public ground response.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is less horizontally extended and should not become an atrium-driven slab.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated massing with a central atrium and folded roof can make a compact commercial/neighborly figure feel open.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more spread out and sectional; candidate should stay compact and not fragment into multiple pavilions.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, connected wings around a core can express a neighborhood building while preserving a clear communal void.
